adds.title: 2026 law lengthening penalties for 'unnatural acts' - Sonko bill adopted March 12, signed by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye March 30
adds.summary: In February 2026 Senegal's government adopted a draft bill to harden repression of same-sex 'acts against nature,' already punishable by 1 to 5 years imprisonment, by raising fines from 1.5 million to 10 million CFA francs and targeting organizations promoting LGBT philosophy via film, television or writing, amid 17 arrests for 'acts against nature' in early February 2026.

adds.title: United Nations Human Rights Council Universal Periodic Reviews of Senegal (2009 and 2013)
adds.summary: Senegal Penal Code Article 319(3) punishes an improper or unnatural act with a person of the same sex with one to five years imprisonment and a fine of 100,000 to 1,500,000 francs, Senegal provides no legal gender recognition procedure, and in the 2009 and 2013 Universal Periodic Reviews Senegal rejected recommendations to decriminalize same-sex conduct and to prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, maintaining criminal liability and enforcement risk.
